what_its_for: Cefepime is an antibiotic used to treat serious bacterial infections. These include infections of the lungs (pneumonia), urinary tract (bladder and kidneys), skin, and bloodstream. It may also be used for certain infections in patients with low white blood cell counts (febrile neutropenia). It works by killing the bacteria causing your infection.
how_to_take: Cefepime is given by a healthcare provider as an injection into a vein (IV) or into a muscle (IM). You will usually receive this medicine in a hospital, clinic, or infusion center. Sometimes it may be given at home by a home health nurse or trained caregiver. Each dose is given slowly over 30 minutes to 1 hour through an IV line. Never try to give this injection to yourself unless you have been fully trained by a healthcare professional. Make sure to complete the full course of treatment even if you start feeling better, so the infection is completely cleared.
dosing: Your dose will be decided by your doctor based on your type of infection, how serious it is, your weight, kidney function, and other health conditions. A typical adult dose is 1 to 2 grams given every 8 to 12 hours, usually for 7 to 14 days. Children's doses are based on body weight. If you have kidney problems, your doctor may lower your dose or change how often you receive it. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions for your dose.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose or your infusion is delayed, contact your doctor, nurse, or home health agency right away. Try to take the missed dose as soon as you remember, unless it is almost time for your next scheduled dose. In that case, skip the missed dose and go back to your regular schedule. Do not double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Cefepime vials (powder) should be stored at room temperature, away from heat and direct light. Once the powder is mixed into a solution, it should be stored in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F / 2°C to 8°C) and used within 24 hours, or at room temperature and used within 12 hours. Frozen solutions can be stored for up to 3 months. Never use a solution that looks cloudy, has particles in it, or has changed color. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children and pets. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet — ask your pharmacist how to safely dispose of it.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol during your treatment and for at least 48 hours after your last dose, as it may cause unpleasant reactions. Tell your doctor about all other medicines you are taking, especially blood thinners like warfarin (Coumadin), other antibiotics, or diuretics (water pills) such as furosemide, as these can interact with cefepime. Do not stop your treatment early without talking to your doctor, even if you feel better.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or get emergency medical help right away if you experience any of the following: severe allergic reaction (rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, difficulty breathing, dizziness); seizures or unusual confusion, especially if you are elderly or have kidney problems; severe or bloody diarrhea that may be watery or have mucus — this could be a sign of a serious bowel infection (C. difficile); signs of a new infection such as a fever; yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice); unusual bruising or bleeding; or any injection site becomes red, swollen, or painful.
when_it_works: You may start to feel better within a few days of starting cefepime, but it is important to finish your entire course of treatment as directed. If your symptoms do not improve after a few days or get worse at any point, contact your doctor.
special_populations: Kidney problems: If your kidneys do not work well, your doctor will adjust your dose to prevent the medicine from building up in your body, which can cause serious side effects like seizures. Older adults (65+): Older patients are more sensitive to cefepime and have a higher risk of side effects such as confusion and seizures. Close monitoring is important. Children: Cefepime can be used in children and infants older than 2 months. The dose is based on body weight and calculated by your doctor. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Cefepime should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed. Small amounts may pass into breast milk, so talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits.
